title: Muscles of the neck (right lateral)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Sternal head: front of the manubrium. Clavicular head: upper surface of the medial third of the clavicle.
Mastoid process of the temporal bone and the lateral half of the superior nuchal line.
Accessory nerve (cranial nerve XI). Branches of C2 and C3 carry its pain and position sense.
One side alone tilts the head toward its own shoulder and turns the face to the opposite side. Both sides together flex the neck.
hy: An accessory nerve lesion weakens turning of the face to the opposite side. A shortened muscle causes torticollis: the head tilts toward that side and the chin turns away from it.

rows: Anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3 to C6.
Scalene tubercle on the upper surface of the 1st rib.
Anterior rami of C4 to C6.
Raises the 1st rib in inspiration. Bends the neck forward and to its own side.
hy: The roots of the brachial plexus and the subclavian artery pass behind it, between it and the middle scalene. The subclavian vein and the phrenic nerve pass in front of it. Narrowing of the gap behind it, for example by a cervical rib, compresses the lower plexus and the artery (thoracic outlet syndrome).

rows: Transverse processes of C2 to C7, from their posterior tubercles.
Upper surface of the 1st rib, behind the groove for the subclavian artery.
Anterior rami of C3 to C8.
Raises the 1st rib in inspiration. Bends the neck to its own side.
Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C4 to C6.
Anterior rami of C6 to C8.
Raises the 2nd rib in inspiration. Bends the neck to its own side.
Transverse processes of C1 to C4.
Medial border of the scapula, from the superior angle to the root of the spine.
Dorsal scapular nerve (C5) and branches of C3 and C4.
Raises the scapula and turns its glenoid cavity downward. With the scapula fixed, bends the neck to its own side.
Lower half of the ligamentum nuchae and spinous processes of C7 to T3.
Mastoid process of the temporal bone and the lateral third of the superior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves.
Both sides together extend the head and neck. One side alone bends the head to that side and turns the face to the same side.
Inferior belly: upper border of the scapula beside the suprascapular notch.
Superior belly: lower border of the body of the hyoid bone. The two bellies meet at an intermediate tendon that a sling of fascia holds down to the clavicle.
Lowers and steadies the hyoid bone after it has been raised in swallowing.
Back of the manubrium and the medial end of the clavicle.
Lower border of the body of the hyoid bone.
Lowers the hyoid bone after it has been raised in swallowing.
Back of the manubrium, below the origin of sternohyoid.
Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
Lowers the larynx after it has been raised in swallowing.
Posterior belly: mastoid notch of the temporal bone. Anterior belly: digastric fossa of the mandible.
The two bellies meet at an intermediate tendon that a fibrous sling holds to the body and greater horn of the hyoid bone.
Anterior belly: nerve to mylohyoid, from the mandibular nerve (V3). Posterior belly: facial nerve (VII).
Raises the hyoid bone in swallowing. With the hyoid fixed, lowers the mandible to open the mouth.
hy: Two bellies with two nerves, because they come from different pharyngeal arches: the anterior belly from the 1st (V3), the posterior belly from the 2nd (VII).

rows: Styloid process of the temporal bone.
Body of the hyoid bone where it meets the greater horn. Its tendon splits around the intermediate tendon of digastric.
Raises the hyoid bone and draws it back in swallowing.
A median raphe running from the mandible to the hyoid, and the body of the hyoid bone.
Nerve to mylohyoid, a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (V3).
The two muscles form the floor of the mouth. They raise the floor of the mouth, the hyoid and the tongue in swallowing and speaking.
